That is a 48-grey-level split inside one control, and it makes 'Search documents' the palest ink in a pane where every other secondary label (dates, previews, 'Sort by Date', '8 documents · 239 words', 'All changes saved') lands on exactly #8C8C8C. B's placeholder is #999999 against a #989898 icon — matched to within one level.
gapTheirs: B runs two secondary greys and two papers across a single hairline. Sidebar chrome and text — toolbar toggle, folder icon, + button, every date, both preview lines, the sort control, the count, the status line — are #999999 on #FDFDFD paper (2.80:1). The document title 'sea-storm.md' in the same 40px toolbar strip, eight pixels across the divider, is #8C8C8C on #F9F9F9. A puts all of it — pane chrome, dates, previews, status line and editor title — on one grey (#8C8C8C) and one paper (#F7F7F7), 3.14:1, so its library is continuous with its page; B's is a second, paler theme bolted to the side of the first.
verdict: A's library and A's page are the same sheet of paper with a line ruled down it; B's library is a slightly whiter card laid on top, set in a slightly weaker grey, and you feel the seam every time your eye crosses it. B's previews are the ones that cost you: at 2.80:1 the two lines under each filename are texture rather than text, and finding the chapter that starts with the gale means opening files instead of reading the list. B also can't hold a straight left edge — its sort label, file icons and search glyph sit at 14.5, 16.5 and 20 logical px, three edges where A has one — and its row pitch alternates 77/78px instead of A's flat 75. A's one real failure is that its search placeholder is a ghost at 1.8:1 next to its own icon at 3.1:1; that is a bad half-hour for one control, not a pane built on two grey ramps.

states.gap: Name and date don't share a baseline: the date's x-height band sits 2 device px (1 CSS px) above the filename's in every row — row 1 baseline 231 (sea-storm) vs 229 (Mar 14, 25), row 2 381 vs 379 — where A lands both on the same baseline exactly.
states.gapTheirs: The list's secondary ink is #999999 on a #FDFDFD pane = 2.80:1, under the 3:1 floor — so the two-line excerpt, the date, 'Sort by Date' and '2 of 8 documents' all read fainter than B's #8C8C8C on #F7F7F7 (3.14:1); the row you scan the library by is the palest thing in the window.
states.verdict: Two near-identical panes, so it comes down to what you actually do with them: read rows and run your eye down a left edge. A sets its excerpts and dates at 2.80:1 on the brightest surface in the app and then indents the search magnifier to x=19.5 while the document icons below sit at 16.5 and the sort label at 14.5 — a three-position rail you can see at half scale. B is straighter and darker where it counts, and pays for it with a 1 px date baseline that floats off the filename and an excerpt that guillotines 'boathouse' into 'boath…'. Neither pane earns trust outright; B is the one whose file list you can read at a glance.
